text:
Sam L.: Quick sync — I'm proposing we bifurcate the feature-gate logic out of tenant-config and run it as a tiny feature-gate service. Goal: smaller blast radius for config churn, independent scaling for feature checks, and simpler rollout surface. Plan sketch below — need opinions before I write an RFC.

Maria P.: +1 to the intent. main worry: tenant-config currently stores both env + flags in one table and some code paths do joins we rely on. We need a migration strategy that doesn't double-read for latency-sensitive hotpaths. :thinking_face:

Aj R.: Proposal: do a read-through cache pattern during migration. New feature-gate service reads flags from its store, falls back to tenant-config via a fast RPC if missing, and we backfill async. That avoids double-writes on the hot path.

Sam L.: Exactly. I sketched a 3-phase plan: 
1) Add feature_flags table and a read-fallback layer in app code (no cutover).
2) Backfill flags from tenant_config into feature_flags async, ramp by tenant cohorts.
3) Flip the app to prefer feature-gate service + incrementally move write paths.

Kevin W.: Who owns the new service? UX/Console team needs to own the admin UI, infra should own runtime SLA. We should map ownership now — otherwise we get the familiar handoff lag.

Ira S.: Observability note: we need per-tenant flag decision traces. Add a small span on each decision and a sampling config for high-qps tenants. Also metric: flag-miss-rate (calls that hit fallback) and miss-latency.

Sam L.: Good call. I added that to the plan: traces + flag-miss-rate. Also thinking about rollout policy: start with 1% of tenants, then 10, then 50. Each step gated by miss-rate < 1% and 99th p90 latency delta < 10ms.

Maria P.: About data ownership: do we keep tenant_config as source-of-truth for a while, or flip truth to feature_flags? I'd prefer source-of-truth flip only after full backfill + 2-week stabilization window.

Aj R.: +1 on flip-after-stabilize. Implementation detail: writes from console go to both stores (dual-write) in transition; background reconciler picks up drift. We should avoid synchronous dual-writes for API paths with tight latency.

Kevin W.: Ops question: what resources? feature-gate is tiny but must be low-latency (sub-5ms cold). Suggest using small dedicated cache tier (in-memory, sharded by tenant hash) + autoscale by qps. Put it behind the request-router with local caching to keep cross-region latencies down.

Sam L.: I'll add infra sizing estimates to the RFC. For the migration we can use a single-step script and then a streaming reconcile job. Draft snippet for backfill job: 
```
COPY (SELECT tenant_id, flags FROM tenant_config WHERE flags IS NOT NULL) TO '/tmp/flags.csv' WITH CSV;
# then importer pushes to feature_flags store with idempotent upserts
```

Ira S.: Make sure the backfill marks a migration_epoch so reconciler can detect which rows were moved during the window. Also add a checksum column so we can detect drift without full compares.

Maria P.: One more thing — access control. feature-gate will need the same RBAC rules as tenant-config admin endpoints. Let's not forget audit logs for flag changes.

Aj R.: Noted. We'll wire KMS/HSM audit hooks and reuse console auth middleware.

deploy-bot: deploy #feature-gate-proto to staging succeeded — 2023-11-02T15:12:05Z :white_check_mark:

Sam L.: Nice — can folks +1 the plan here or drop objections. If none, I'll start an RFC draft and tag owners for ownership mapping.

Kevin W.: +1. I can take infra sizing & runbook.

Maria P.: +1 from me, will prep migration checklist items for console.

Ira S.: +1 on observability parts, will mock dashboards.

Aj R.: +1, will pair on reconciler design.

Sam L.: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC by EOD tomorrow and include the ramp criteria and metrics we discussed. :rocket:
